clue.text: Undergo punishment, suffering at length? Untrue

indicators.note: something suffering is battered out of shape, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone endures a long ordeal, and the clue then calls the claim false.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'suffering' sits at the start and acts on both 'at length' and 'Untrue', even though the question mark seems to split them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from an old military penalty of passing between two lines of men who struck the offender.

clue.text: Brown's old city entertaining honoured member

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them inside, so the city's letters go around the honour

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
an MBE is a Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: An ancient city belonging to someone called Brown hosts a person given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown's' reads as a man's name; it is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy pigment giving a dark yellowish-brown colour.

clue.text: Muddy and difficult course to the north? Propose to go south

indicators.note: in a down entry south means lower down, so this piece is placed beneath the first
in a down clue, going north means reading the letters upwards, so the word is written back to front

parts.note: a rut is a groove a wheel gets stuck in, a hard course to escape
to bid is to propose or offer

explanation.surface: A rough cross-country course runs north while someone suggests heading south instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns RUT upwards into TUR; 'to go south' places BID below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbid water is cloudy with stirred-up sediment, so it is thick and murky.

clue.text: More than one agent stars — negligent, not right, to begin with

indicators.note: this places the trimmed negligent word at the start, ahead of the stars
not having something means it is left out, so the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: remiss means careless or negligent
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: An agency complains that its agents are careless stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like the celebrity agents' clients, but it is the zodiac constellation; 'to begin with' sets the trimmed word first.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys sent on a mission, so several of them are agents acting for someone.

clue.text: Take off by the highest point

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic them, to take them off
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' (three by four)

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes off and climbs to its ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' sounds like flight but means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the peak or summit, the topmost tip of something.

clue.text: Old stone implement damaged the 15

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 15, the big cat

explanation.surface: An ancient stone tool has been harmed by a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points to the answer at 15-across; its four letters join THE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone tool or weapon of the New Stone Age.

clue.text: Royal house with endless territory and a Roller

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is cut off

parts.note: land is territory
a caster is a small swivelling wheel under furniture, something that rolls

explanation.surface: A royal family owns vast estates and a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Roller' looks like slang for a Rolls-Royce car; it is a furniture wheel, also spelt castor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster was the English dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI, one side in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Are trips chosen to be choreographed for them?

definitions.text: Are trips chosen to be choreographed for them?

indicators.note: choreographing arranges dancers' steps, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Dance steps ('trips') are picked and arranged for certain performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Trips here are light dance steps; the whole clue both builds and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Muse of dance, so her followers are dancers, for whom steps are choreographed.

clue.text: Teacher of history maybe in after-school bar getting drunk

indicators.note: someone getting drunk is all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher goes to the pub after lessons and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks a history teacher as one example of a holder of this degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanities graduate holds this first degree, which is typical of someone who teaches history.

clue.text: Something eaten at home, boxed by foreign eaterie

indicators.note: something boxed by another is enclosed within it, so the inn's letters surround the home piece

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn or restaurant
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: Diners eat in at home, but the meal comes from a foreign restaurant in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, or eggplant, is a purple vegetable that is cooked and eaten.

clue.text: Proprietor to acknowledge one deserving royal treatment

parts.note: to own is to admit or acknowledge
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A shop proprietor greets a customer who deserves red-carpet treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who possesses a business or property.

clue.text: Retired folk that woman's seen outside US university

indicators.note: being outside another piece means wrapping around it

parts.note: hers means belonging to that woman
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Pensioners spot a woman outside an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means withdrawn from society, not pensioned off.
explanation.definitionFit: Recluses who withdraw from the world are retiring in the sense of secluded.

clue.text: Furniture I had brought back by suitable transport?

indicators.note: bringing something back turns it around, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
vans are the right vehicles for moving furniture

explanation.surface: Someone had furniture delivered back in the right vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Divans are low beds or couches, items of furniture.

clue.text: Eager desire that could be a feature of hotel initially

definitions.text: that could be a feature of hotel initially
definitions.meaning: the breathed H sound at the start of 'hotel', pronounced by all but cockneys and the French

explanation.surface: Ambition might drive someone to own a hotel at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a strong ambition and the breathy sound of an initial H in phonetics share this word.

clue.text: Number one animal ultimately — that about it?

definitions.text: Number one animal ultimately — that about it?

indicators.note: 'that' gathers the pieces just built, and 'about' turns them round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word animal

explanation.surface: The question asks if the king of beasts sums it all up.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I and L give NOIL, which 'about' turns round; the whole clue also describes the king of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is traditionally called the king of beasts, the top animal.

clue.text: Meet actor struggling with long line of verse

indicators.note: struggling suggests flailing about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer has trouble with a long line in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An octameter is a line of poetry with eight metrical feet, a very long line.

clue.text: Article fitted in giving support, something wooden mostly — peg leg?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: an item fitted in another goes inside it
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a stick is a piece of wood
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A wooden support with a fitted part, nearly all wood: a pirate's peg leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving support' is not the definition; it is the argument word for 'in favour'. The question mark flags the peg leg as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg leg is a crude artificial limb, the sort of replacement body part this word describes.

clue.text: Mad sister and I tucked into caviar maybe in restaurant

indicators.note: tucked into a piece means placed inside it

parts.note: caviar is one kind of roe, fish eggs

indicators.note: mad suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A crazy sister and the speaker tuck into caviar at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' scrambles the sister and I into TISSERI, which 'tucked into' places between RO and E of the fish eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a spit, this word names a restaurant specialising in spit-roasted meats.

clue.text: Celebrated with song uplifting wine

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it in verse, so sang means celebrated

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up reads the letters upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: People celebrated with a rousing song and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' looks like praise for the song, but it turns AIR upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit.

clue.text: Musical piece from choir turning around

indicators.note: around means the extracted letters are turned back to front
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A short piece of music comes from a choir turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a composition written for three players or voices.

clue.text: Grandma hugged by Margaret in in a state

indicators.note: held in a hug, the grandmother sits inside the other name

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret
Nan is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother gets hugged by Margaret while she is in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as upset, but 'a state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is one of the constituent states of Malaysia.

clue.text: Provoke old fellows to wear something pink

indicators.note: wearing something means being inside it, so these pieces go within the pink item

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is printed on pink paper
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Old chaps are goaded into wearing something pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times, a London business newspaper, is known for its pink pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to stir it up or incite it.

clue.text: Plant with unusual name presented to somebody

indicators.note: unusual signals letters in an odd order

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one must'

explanation.surface: A plant with a strange name is given to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family, also called windflower.

clue.text: Disgust shown by element wanting leader gone

indicators.note: with its leader gone, the first letter is removed

parts.note: sodium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Revulsion is shown by a chemical element that wants its leader removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is hatred and contempt felt widely toward someone.

clue.text: Plans set up to provide rationed food?

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written upwards, back to front

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Plans are drawn up to supply rations.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an example: Spam, a tinned meat, was a staple during British wartime rationing.
explanation.definitionFit: This canned pork luncheon meat was a wartime staple eaten under rationing.

clue.text: What goes round can go round in reverse

definitions.note: a rotating blade or drum, the part of a machine that spins; this same word reads identically from either end

indicators.note: the word can be read backwards to give the same thing, a palindrome

parts.note: a rotating blade or drum, the part of a machine that spins; this same word reads identically from either end

explanation.surface: Something that spins can spin the other way too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' first means spin, then turn the word about; it reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as helicopter blades.

clue.text: Quietly helping four being imprisoned in state of hardship

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: imprisoned in a word means put inside it

parts.note: a ration is a share or helping
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four prisoners quietly helped one another in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Privation is a lack of the basic necessities of life, so it is a condition of want.

clue.text: It involves a sequence of matches

definitions.text: It involves a sequence of matches

parts.words: It involves a sequence of matches
parts.note: the matches are romantic pairings, not games, made one after another

explanation.surface: It sounds like a sports tournament or a fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: This means having one exclusive partner at a time, moving through a succession of relationships.
